prerequisites: In-depth knowledge of an object-oriented programming language covered in previous basic modules.
Basic prior knowledge of object-oriented design, development of distributed systems, and software architecture in general is helpful, but not required.

learning_outcomes.text: Students who have successfully completed this module can appropriately design, implement, test, provide, and adapt interfaces of classes, packages, modules, components, and services.
Students who have successfully completed this module can justify the importance and impact of interface design.
Students who have successfully completed this module can integrate existing software components via defined interfaces.
Students who have successfully completed this module can design and implement interfaces.
Students who have successfully completed this module can characterize interfaces with regard to requested quality features.
Students who have successfully completed this module can estimate and evaluate the quality of APIs.
Students who have successfully completed this module can explain the effects of decisions on an API and its use.
Students who have successfully completed this module can assess the advantages and disadvantages of used patterns and best practices.
Students who have successfully completed this module can realize appropriate interfaces at different levels of a software from conception to provision and maintenance.
Students who have successfully completed this module can determine requirements for the interface of a program or a software component from developers.
Students who have successfully completed this module can document the programming interface of a program / software component and explain it to software architects and developers in discussions.
Students can design appropriate programming interfaces.

assessment_rules: Graded assessment can be a term paper, presentation with written elaboration, or a written project report. The form of assessment is determined by the lecturer in accordance with the valid study regulations. Ungraded assessments include experimental work (approx. 8 experiments in total) or regular participation (at least 80% attendance). For graded assessments, a term paper is approx. 15-20 pages with a possible 15-minute explanation; a presentation is approx. 15-20 minutes with an 8-10 page elaboration; a project report is approx. 10-15 pages with a possible 15-minute explanation.
